title: Federated learning for atrial fibrillation detection across heterogeneous wearable ECG devices

record.title: Federated learning for atrial fibrillation detection across heterogeneous wearable ECG devices
record.abstract: Training robust atrial fibrillation detectors on data pooled from multiple clinical sites raises significant patient privacy concerns. Federated learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving alternative by training shared model parameters without centralizing raw recordings. This work presents a federated AF detection framework tailored to the heterogeneous signal characteristics encountered when aggregating data from four distinct wearable ECG patch platforms with differing sampling rates, electrode configurations, and noise profiles. A domain-adaptive normalization layer is inserted before each local model head to compensate for device-specific distributional shifts. Communication efficiency is improved through gradient sparsification with a threshold calibrated per round. Experiments conducted on data partitioned across five simulated client nodes demonstrate that the federated model achieves within 2.1 percentage points of a centrally trained oracle in terms of F1 score for AF detection, while keeping raw data entirely local. Convergence analysis shows stable training within 35 communication rounds. The proposed approach is directly applicable to collaborative model development between hospitals and medical device manufacturers operating under strict data governance constraints.
